# template-manifest.txt — WHO OWNS WHAT in your office
#
# The law this file exists to enforce:
#
#     Factory updates the operating system.
#     It does not redecorate the customer's office.
#
#     OFFICE IS THE DEFAULT. CORE IS A NARROW ALLOWLIST.
#
# The factory-update workflow reads THIS file — your copy — and syncs only what
# it names, always as a pull request you review and merge. Every managed path
# carries an owner, and the owner decides what an update may do to it.
#
# ── The bar for `core` ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# A path is Factory-owned ONLY when SquidBay must stay authoritative over that
# exact material for the Factory framework to work correctly across every
# installation. Not "it's important." Not "we wrote it." Not "it would be nice
# if everyone had the current one." Mechanical necessity, or it is yours.
#
# Everything else is yours after installation: human-editable content, defaults,
# company and process material, operational prose, examples, organisational
# instructions, and anything a customer could reasonably be expected to
# personalise. That includes every seat's boot material, your onboarding, your
# templates and forms, your specialist and tool descriptions, your hosting notes,
# your token model, your local SECURITY and CONTRIBUTING policy, your README and
# office identity, your mission packs, and your rulebook.
#
# ── The two owners ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
#   core PATH       FACTORY-OWNED. Arrives by OVERWRITE, every run. The list
#                   below is the whole of it, and every line carries its reason.
#
#   office PATH     OFFICE-OWNED AFTER INSTALLATION. SEEDED once if your office
#                   does not have it yet, then NEVER written again. If the
#                   Factory's default later improves, the update PR NAMES the
#                   file as a migration proposal — and still does not write it.
#                   Your customisation is safe by architecture, not by your
#                   having remembered to protect it.
#
#   PATH            A bare line with no owner word means `core`. This is a
#                   PARSER fallback for manifests written before ownership
#                   existed, so no older office silently stops receiving updates
#                   — it is NOT the policy. The policy is the line at the top:
#                   office is the default. This file therefore contains ZERO
#                   bare lines, and the `update-engine` workflow fails the build
#                   if one appears, so the allowlist cannot grow by accident.
#
#   !PATH           PROTECTED — never written, whatever its owner. Your own
#                   local opt-out for a `core` file you have deliberately made
#                   your own. It is a convenience, not a defence: ownership is
#                   the defence, and a growing pile of "!" lines is the symptom
#                   of a classification that needs fixing upstream instead.
#
# Anything NOT listed here is yours alone: never seeded, never touched, never
# mentioned. Your journal, your specs, your roster, your company knowledge, and
# every file you add.
#
# One path per line. A trailing slash means "the whole folder." Lines starting
# with # are comments.
#
# ── Which rule applies to a file: the LONGEST match wins ─────────────────────
# The most specific rule decides. That is what keeps a narrow Factory-owned
# contract inside a broad Office-owned tree — see the seat loaders below — and
# it is why a whole directory is never made Core just because one small thing
# inside it is framework machinery. Order in this file does not matter, only
# specificity, so a manifest cannot be broken by moving a line.
#
# ── Two things the sync can never do to you ──────────────────────────────────
#   • It never DELETES. A file of yours the Factory has never heard of is left
#     alone, not removed. (An earlier version `rm -rf`'d each managed folder and
#     re-copied it, which silently deleted every office-only file inside.)
#   • It never overwrites an `office` path, and never writes a `!` path.


# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# CORE — the allowlist. Seven lines. Each one has to earn its place.
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# The updater's own engine and its two proofs. factory-update.yml EXECUTES
# scripts/factory-sync.sh, and runs scripts/sync-selftest.sh and
# scripts/ownership-rehearsal.sh as gates before it will sync anything. The
# workflow and the code it runs are ONE subsystem: if the scripts are not
# Factory-owned, a fix to the sync engine lands upstream and stops at your door
# in silence while your workflow keeps running the old one. This is the clearest
# case of mechanical necessity in the repository.
core scripts/

# How your office knows which Factory version it is on. The update check reads
# it; a stale or office-edited copy makes the check lie in either direction.
core .github/template-version.txt

# The update system's own delivery channel — the release note for each update,
# written by the Factory, for you. The page itself says the office never writes
# here and your memory lives in journal.md instead. Seeded-once would mean a
# news feed that delivers news exactly once, which is not a news feed. This is
# the one Core line that is prose rather than machinery, and that is its reason.
core FROM-HQ.md

# The four thin seat loaders — the small stable cards installed in Claude's
# settings that do nothing but point at this repo. They are a CONTRACT, not
# content: they must keep working when the boot material behind them changes,
# and that material (BOOT-PROMPT.md, GROUNDING.md, OVERRIDES.md, and anything
# your office adds beside them) is yours under `office seats/` below. This pair
# of rules is the longest-match mechanism doing the job it exists for.
#
# (These four directories still carry their original names. The campaign's card
# rename to coach / team-leader / engineer / creative-director moves these four
# lines with them; it is a later step and deliberately not done here.)
core seats/coach/coach-boot/
core seats/cowork/cowork-boot/
core seats/designer/designer-boot/
core seats/worker/worker-boot/


# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# OFFICE — everything else the Factory ships. Yours from the moment it lands.
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# Your seats. Boot prompts, grounding, overrides, shared boot material, local
# doctrine — the most customised material in any office, and the reason this
# whole boundary exists. The four loaders above are the only exceptions.
office seats/

# The Engineer seat's boot material, which lives at the repo root because
# attaching the repo to Claude Code loads it automatically. It is a boot prompt
# like the other three seats', and it is yours for the same reason theirs are.
# The auto-load itself is Claude Code's contract about the FILENAME and costs
# nothing to keep: it holds whatever the file says.
office CLAUDE.md

# The rulebook that binds your seats' behaviour. Human-editable operational
# policy — offices sharpen, add to, and reword these. The Factory's improvements
# reach you as named migration proposals, not as overwrites of your rules.
office MECHANICAL-RULES.md

# Your office's identity and descriptive content, its verification log, and its
# own third-party notices about its own repository.
office README.md
office VERSIONS.md
office THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md

# Your LOCAL policy for your own repository, not the Factory's.
office .github/CONTRIBUTING.md
office .github/SECURITY.md

# What your seats read to know your world.
office grounding/

# Operational prose your office adapts: the guides, the onboarding path, the
# templates and forms you fill in, the specialist and tool descriptions, the
# hosting notes you point at your own infrastructure, your token and business
# model, and the versions pages.
office guides/
office onboarding/
office templates/
office specialists/
office hosting/
office tokens/
office versions/

# The missions — a shipped mission is a starting point you rewrite for the way
# your office actually works.
office missions/

# The shipped skills. Capabilities your office adapts; an edit of yours is not
# reclaimed because the Factory improved its own copy.
office skills/

# The README files that explain a folder's convention to whoever opens it.
office inbox/drop/README.md
office journal/README.md
office specs/README.md


# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Deliberately absent — never seeded, never synced, never mentioned:
#   FACTORY.md            (carries your roster and your names)
#   journal.md            (your team's memory — the Factory's own news rides
#                          the Core-owned FROM-HQ.md instead, never journal.md)
#   journal/archive/      (your history)
#   specs/                (your plans; only its README is managed)
#   .github/guardrails-denylist.txt  (your private-name denylist)
#   .github/heartbeat-watch.txt      (your own nightly watch list)
#   .github/template-manifest.txt    (THIS file — deciding who owns a path is a
#                          choice only you may make. The update run reports it
#                          as drift and never writes it.)
#   .github/workflows/    (a repo's automation can't be rewritten by its own
#                          automation — workflow changes arrive as a note in the
#                          update PR for an Engineer seat to apply. This is the
#                          ONE part of the updater that cannot be synced. Its
#                          engine, scripts/, is Core above, so the hand-carry is
#                          the workflow files alone — and
#                          guides/SAFE-UPDATE-BOOTSTRAP.md is the order to do it
#                          in, for an office that still has the old one.)
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
